quarterly_data.signal: CFO Wissam Jabre: Q4 product revenue of $966 million was up 14% year-over-year, driven by the execution of a multi-year agreement with Google Cloud to deliver secure AI-ready data infrastructure to Google Distributed Cloud environments - the large deals NetApp had flagged for the second half of fiscal 2026 came to fruition in Q4. Product gross margin was 56.1%, up 80 basis points sequentially, as the benefit from the Google Cloud agreement offset higher component costs.
quarterly_data.figure: product revenue up 14% year-over-year; product gross margin up 80 basis points sequentially

quarterly_data.signal: AI demand: CEO George Kurian said NetApp had approximately 500 AI and data preparation wins in Q4 alone, bringing the FY 2026 total to over 1,100, compared with roughly 400 for the whole of the prior fiscal year. All of the Q4 AI wins were on-prem (a mix of enterprise and neo cloud); about half are data preparation / large-scale analytics now run under GPU compute and the rest split roughly evenly between LLM training/fine-tuning and inferencing ('roughly 50/25/25'), a pattern stable through the year. All-flash grew particularly in AI use cases, while customers in non-demanding AI environments are starting to buy more hybrid flash.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 500 AI and data preparation wins in Q4; over 1,100 in FY 2026 vs roughly 400 in the prior fiscal year

quarterly_data.signal: Public cloud: FY 2026 public cloud revenue grew to $688 million, up 18% (normalized for the Spot divestiture), driven by first-party and marketplace cloud services (NetApp storage services on AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud) that increased 30%. Q4 public cloud revenue was $182 million, up 11% (18% excluding Spot), with public cloud gross margin of 85.7%, above the 80%-85% long-term target range for the last two quarters. Kurian expects cloud to grow faster in FY2027 than in FY2026 and is starting to see AI use cases show up in the cloud.
quarterly_data.figure: FY 2026 public cloud revenue $688 million, up 18%; first-party and marketplace services up 30%; Q4 public cloud up 18% excluding Spot; public cloud gross margin 85.7%

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog: NetApp exited fiscal 2026 with $4.85 billion in deferred revenue (an increase of 7%) and unbilled remaining performance obligations - a key indicator of future Keystone storage-as-a-service revenue - of $807 million, up 88% year-over-year, driven by support performance obligations tied to the Google agreement plus Keystone unbilled RPO. Keystone revenue grew approximately 65% from FY 2025, and all-flash reached 48% of the installed base (up another 1%).
quarterly_data.figure: unbilled RPO $807 million, up 88%; deferred revenue $4.85 billion; Keystone revenue up approximately 65%; all-flash 48% of the installed base

quarterly_data.signal: Component-cost inflation (DRAM, NAND): Jabre said the 'July quarter is more or less the trough' for product gross margin, with gradual improvement expected as price adjustments taken against rising component costs take effect through the year; NAND prices show up mainly in product gross margin (Keystone less affected as it is recognized over time). Kurian said NetApp raised prices during Q4 but it had not yet materially flowed into recorded transactions - historically this has taken about three quarters, and it should flow through over the next quarter to two. The long-term product gross margin target stays at mid 50% to high 50%. Pull-forward impact on the Q4 P&L was minimal, though management sees some accelerated decision-making.
quarterly_data.figure: long-term product gross margin target mid 50% to high 50%

quarterly_data.signal: Supply: asked about constraints beyond NAND, hard drives and DRAM, Kurian said NetApp works with multiple suppliers for pretty much every component, is cognizant that there could be constraints in other parts of the ecosystem, and that one thing clients have talked to NetApp about is HDDs (NetApp has a strong set of HDD-based solutions);'at this time, we believe we can source adequate supply to meet our outlook for the year.' NetApp's goal is to balance cost and availability of supply and keep lead times within customers' normal expectations.

FY2027 guidance mechanics: the $7.45 billion midpoint implies 8% growth, an acceleration from 5% in FY2026, and the Q1 midpoint implies 17% growth; Q1 includes an extra week expected to add approximately $65 million of revenue (mainly support and cloud, minimal product impact) and $21 million of operating expenses. Adjusting for the extra week, the first-half/second-half split is roughly seasonal, and Q2-Q4 implies mid-single digit percent growth. Guidance assumes a solid enterprise IT demand environment with enterprise AI activity increasing versus FY2026, possible pockets of accelerated purchasing, and pricing adjusted to track memory and component costs.
quarterly_data.figure: extra week in Q1: approximately $65 million of revenue and $21 million of operating expenses

quarterly_data.signal: AI product ramps: AFX (disaggregated all-flash) has good wins in Neo cloud, financial services, hedge funds and life sciences and more customers are qualifying it, though as a new architecture it will take time; AI Data Engine (AIDE) is getting good early feedback, monetized standalone or bundled with storage. A top five U.S. neo cloud chose NetApp as the platform for high-performance enterprise AI use cases; NetApp fueled nearly 50 partner AI factories and labs (e.g. AFX at World Wide Technology's AI proving ground); a global financial leader signed a $20 million deal for a GPU-ready data lake platform. NetApp built a specialist AI sales team targeting neo and sovereign clouds.
quarterly_data.figure: top five U.S. neo cloud win; nearly 50 partner AI factories and labs; $20 million deal

contracts.signal: NetApp executed a multi-year agreement with Google Cloud to deliver secure AI-ready data infrastructure to Google Distributed Cloud environments, which drove Q4 product revenue growth and support performance obligations; Kurian: 'NetApp was chosen by Google to be a large chunk of the data infrastructure within the Google Distributed Cloud architecture' (disconnected or lightly connected data centers for regulated industries, public sector and national security), an expansion of work with Google since 2024. Jabre: the agreement sits in the hybrid cloud segment and will also help support revenue going forward.
contracts.date_signed: executed in Q4 FY2026 (signing date not stated)

contracts.signal: A European government agency needing real-time situational awareness deployed NetApp's disaggregated AFX solution for their NVIDIA SuperPOD environment, enabling independent scaling of compute and storage.
An Asian engineering company streamlined its GenAI chatbot deployment on AWS by leveraging FSx for NetApp ONTAP, with permission-aware access to data in place.
A leading insurance company accelerated financial risk modeling and data science by connecting Azure Databricks directly to its data in Azure NetApp Files.
